title: Policy telemetry: compact per-path recording and fanout audit logs
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Smart routing (region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants) currently emits verbose hop-by-hop verbatim traces which increase storage, raise privacy concerns, and make SLO-aligned RCA slow. Goal: produce a compact, structured per-request path record that preserves explainability and replayability for debugging and SLO attribution while minimizing size and sensitive data exposure.

Scope: implement a new Policy Fanout Audit Log format and collection pipeline: (1) per-request compact path record (one line/event per request) that summarizes the routing tree and final verdicts; (2) optional per-hop micro-metrics stream for high-fidelity debugging (sampled); (3) deterministic sampling & TTL for full snapshots; (4) masking/redaction rules and retention limits for PIIs and customer content.

Design constraints and success metrics: compact record size target <= 1.5 KB per request (95th), cost <30% of current tracing bill for routing traces, end-to-end SLO attribution accuracy >= 99% (ability to map latencies and errors to a route leg), and ability to reconstruct fallback chain for any request with sampling guarantees.

Trade-offs being considered:
- Compression vs queryability: heavy protobuf + gzip reduces storage but complicates ad-hoc queries in the Console. We propose primary storage as compressed blobs with an indexed denormalized summary for fast queries.
- Sampling policy complexity: sticky sampling per-customer vs global reservoir sampling. Sticky sampling gives better per-customer debugging at expense of implementation complexity. Plan: start with a hybrid: deterministic hash-based sticky sampling for accounts with high volume, reservoir sampling for low-volume accounts.
- Privacy: redact request text by default; support allowlist for customers who opt-in to high-fidelity recordings. KMS-encrypted blobs will be available for enterprise-only private deployments.

Schema sketch (compact path record as single-line JSON for ingestion - example below will be stored compressed):
{
  "request_id": "uuid",
  "ts": "2026-03-10T14:22:33Z",
  "policy_version": "v4.3.1",
  "route_summary": ["region:us-east-1","tier:dedicated","model_variant:m1-quant"],
  "final_verdict": "served",
  "latency_ms": 72,
  "cost_units": 0.013,
  "fallback_chain": ["m1-quant","m1-fp16","m2-quant"],
  "sample_level": "summary",
  "hash_sample_seed": "0x3af2",
  "masked_top_k_prompts": ["<redacted>"]
}

Implementation plan:
1) Define canonical compact record schema and denormalized query index fields (request_id, ts, region, tier, model_variant, final_verdict, latency_bucket, sampling_tag). (Owner: Javier)
2) Implement runtime emitter with fanout-aware aggregation: when a request is fanned out to N backends, emitter will collapse per-hop metadata into a minimal path vector and compute provenance fingerprint. (Owner: runtime team)
3) Build ingestion pipeline: compressed blob store (S3), indexer (Kafka->Indexer service) to populate the query index used by Console. (Owner: infra/observability)
4) Add per-hop micro-metrics stream for sampled requests; wire into tracing on demand for live debug. (Owner: tracing team)
5) Console integration: new Console view for Path Records, filter by sampling_tag/account/region/tier, and a replay helper that can re-emit a synthetic routed request to staging. (Owner: console)

Open questions:
- What retention policy should apply to index rows vs compressed blobs? Propose 90 days index, 365 days encrypted blob for enterprise only.
- How to represent branching fanouts where model variants are executed in parallel and winner-takes-all? Will encode branch events and the selection fingerprint.
- Rate limits for sampled full snapshots to avoid amplification in incidents.

Risks:
- Incorrect fingerprinting could break correlation with request logs; will add end-to-end verification tests.
- Privacy leak if redaction rules miss tokens; will include automated regex plus ML PII detection before committing blobs.

Links: design doc and proto drafts attached in attachments and PRs for early prototypes.
